subsystems.name: Light collector
subsystems.role: gathers photons from a target star over a large area so that very brief flashes can be detected.

subsystems.name: Fast photodetector
subsystems.role: converts individual photons into electrical pulses with nanosecond timing resolution.

subsystems.name: Coincidence and trigger electronics
subsystems.role: requires simultaneous hits in multiple telescopes to reject cosmic-ray-induced flashes.

subsystems.name: Data acquisition and control
subsystems.role: records candidate events and manages telescope pointing and observation schedule.

subsystems.name: Background rejection
subsystems.role: separates true laser pulses from natural astrophysical variability and atmospheric effects.

buildSteps.title: Select and site telescopes
buildSteps.detail: Choose existing Cherenkov arrays or dedicated optical telescopes in dark, dry locations with good weather and low light pollution.

buildSteps.title: Install fast photodetectors
buildSteps.detail: Mount PMTs or APDs at the focal plane, sometimes behind a beamsplitter to allow simultaneous multi-wavelength or multi-detector coverage.

buildSteps.title: Add timing and coincidence hardware
buildSteps.detail: Equip each telescope with GPS-disciplined clocks and fast discriminators to timestamp photon arrivals to nanosecond precision.

buildSteps.title: Connect telescopes into a coincidence network
buildSteps.detail: Link signals from multiple telescopes so that only near-simultaneous detections, within tens of nanoseconds, are recorded.

buildSteps.title: Commission and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Use pulsed laser tests and cosmic-ray events to measure timing offsets and detection efficiency across the array.

buildSteps.title: Run observations
buildSteps.detail: Point at nearby stars and record any nanosecond pulses, storing data for offline analysis.

buildSteps.title: Analyze data
buildSteps.detail: Search for pulses that repeat or match expected laser signatures, and rule out instrumental and atmospheric artifacts.

prerequisites.tech: Large optical telescopes or mirror arrays
prerequisites.why: collects enough photons from distant stars to detect brief flashes.
resolves laser pulses that last only a few nanoseconds.
distinguishes true pulses from cosmic-ray flashes that hit multiple telescopes.
records and processes high-rate event data in real time or near real time.

pathway.milestone: optical SETI searches on a small number of Cherenkov arrays and dedicated telescopes
pathway.unlocks: limits on artificial laser beacons within tens of light-years of Earth.

pathway.milestone: expansion to more telescopes and wider sky coverage
pathway.unlocks: increased chance of detection and continuous monitoring of nearby stars.

pathway.milestone: dedicated global network with standardized hardware and real-time alerts
pathway.unlocks: rapid follow-up and independent confirmation of candidate signals.

pathway.milestone: integration with radio and infrared SETI for multi-wavelength searches
pathway.unlocks: a more comprehensive survey of potential technosignatures.
